## sections

This guide is the format. What to write and in which form is yuzuno_guide topic brief ("Write for Home"): one conclusion first, important limits beside it, each fact in one place, and execution evidence (logs, raw data, full test output, run and PR lists) left on its Task and linked.

What goes where: Home: a lasting finding, decision or stage result goes in a short report linked to its Task and sources; a current state in a status; a choice for the user in an ask. A yuzuno-ui block in your reply shows only in the conversation. How to write it: yuzuno_guide brief. Update a section when something changed, not every turn; a status past its validFor shows as stale until new facts refresh it. Details stay on the Task and its sources.

A Project's leads edit its Home; the user chooses them. brief_get returns you.capabilities. When editContent is false and writeOwnAsk is true, only create/update/resolve/remove your own Asks, remove your own older sections, or send noChange; do not claim sections, convert regular content into an Ask, or write reports/status. When writeOwnAsk is false, this Brief is read-only, including no noChange writes. Ownership rules still apply to editors. Hidden old content remains in team details/history.
brief_update takes changes: [...]. put creates or replaces one section you own:
- put {op:"put", key, kind: ask|report|status, title, body{…}, ask?{…}, status?{…}, time?{…}, attachments?[≤12]{…}, task?: string|null}

- key: topic or topic/sub; each part 1-48 of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit (round-12, round-12/review). A Brief has at most 12 topics with 4 subs each; a card of an open Task (a topic whose own section has task) does not count, one per Task: it leaves with its Task.

- kind: ask (a question for the user, see ask); report (a result the user reads and marks seen; a report the user marks seen at its latest version leaves brief_get's sections and your ownsKeys at once (a newer version stays, unseen) and stays in Home's history 30 days: put it again under its key to continue it on Home, as edit needs a live section); status (current state; needs status {asOf, validFor}, validFor 60-31536000 seconds; greyed once asOf + validFor has passed). While a conclusion still moves, keep it in a status and refresh it with new facts; once a claim settles, write it as a report under its own key linked to its Task, which the user marks seen and history keeps, and let the status point to it or drop it. A status keeps only its current version: putting it again replaces the earlier wording.
- title: 1-120 characters. body: {root, elements}, see content. time: due, eta and nextUpdate, ISO 8601 with a time zone. attachments: see attachments.

- task (a lead's put or edit; edit may send task alone, without elements): the Task this section is the card of, by its key (YN-90, T-12): a Task of this Project that is not archived, else invalid_task. A put without task keeps the section's Task, every version keeps it, and task:null unbinds it. brief_get and Home then show card {task {id, title, shortName, status, archived}, responsible}: who answers for it now, the Task's newest executor not yet released, else its assignee; the user's replies to the card go to them. A sub-topic under a card is that Task's too, and an executor's own asks and an ask whose gate names a Task show that Task's card. When the Task becomes done or cancelled, or is archived, its card and the sub-topics under it leave the live Brief with reason archived: a report the user has not read in its current version stays until they open it or mark it seen, and an unresolved ask stays until its owner resolves it. A new dispatch of the same Task keeps the card; its new executor answers for it.

- A card's responsible executor (its Task's newest executor not yet released) may put, edit and patch report and status sub-topics under the card's topic (its-topic/result), which are its own and show with the card; anywhere else such a write of an executor's is refused with not_card_responsible.

- markdown instead of body, for a section that is text: Core makes the body one Markdown block "text" under the BriefBody, then "files", an Attachments block of every registered attachment; size (small, wide, large) names the card's size, as summary {lead:"text", size}. Give body or markdown, not both. It works for every kind: an ask's explanation, a status's state. A later edit or patch reaches the text at /elements/text/props/text, e.g. {op:"put", key:"release", kind:"report", title:"core.25 is out", markdown:"**core.25** is installed; the two regressions are fixed in core.26.", size:"small"}.

edit {op:"edit", key, elements:{<id>: {type, props, children?}}, status?} replaces blocks of a section you own by id and keeps the rest as it was: the other blocks and their order, title, attachments, time and the ask's state. Each id is one the body already has, or a new block named as a child by a block you edit; the root is not edited (rearrange with put). Core checks the whole section again. status (kind status only) refreshes asOf. Day to day, edit the blocks that changed, e.g. {op:"edit", key:"overview", elements:{progress:{type:"Plan", props:{steps:[...]}}}}; put a section to create it or change its layout.

patch {op:"patch", key, patch:[...], status?} changes single values of a section you own by RFC 6902 operations (add, remove, replace, move, copy, test) on its body; each path (and from) is a JSON Pointer into body, e.g. {op:"patch", key:"work", patch:[{op:"replace", path:"/elements/tasks/props/items/1/note", value:"Merged."}]}. On an array, @<id> names its one item whose id is <id> wherever an index can go, so the path stays right when items are added or reordered: /elements/runs/props/rows/@r8/cells/status is the status of row r8; as the last token of add it is the place before that item. Indices, - and object keys mean what they always do (on an object @x is the key "@x"), and an id is unescaped like any token (~1 is /). It keeps what edit keeps and Core checks the whole section again; it may also add a block and name it under the root (/elements/<id>, then /elements/<root>/children/-). Operations apply in order; a path or from that is not in the body (an @<id> that names no item, or two), a from of "" (the whole body) for move or copy, or a test whose value differs, refuses the change (patch_path, patch_test), and so does a patch that would build a body far over the limit (too_large); nothing is changed then. Use it for one note, one state or one value; edit to replace whole blocks; put to create a section or change its title.

Other changes: {op:"resolve", key} resolves your ask; {op:"remove", key} removes your section (reports and status go to history); {op:"claim", key} takes an orphaned section of your Project; change it in a later brief_update, not in the one that claims it.

brief_get's you.recentlyLeft lists your sections that left the live Brief in the last 30 days and are not live again, newest first, at most 20: {key, kind, title, version, reason, at}, reason seen (the user marked that version seen), removed, resolved or archived (the Task of its card ended); recentlyLeftMore counts the rest. An edit, resolve, remove or claim naming one of them is refused with not_found, saying why it left; put writes it again.
Only a section's owner changes it. To add to another Agent's section, put your own section under its key as topic/sub; Home shows them together with each author.

Pass expectedVersion from brief_get. On version_conflict the rejection includes latest: the Brief's version, the sections you change as they are now and every section's index entry (brief_get keys reads any other whole); merge and retry with a new requestId. Nothing requires an update each turn; noChange:true is still accepted and changes nothing.

validateOnly:true pre-checks a brief_update: it runs the checks made before the write, with their problems as the update would give them (and latest), and writes nothing: no requestId kept, no version or space reserved, and it is not your update. Its answer has valid, whether the pre-check passed, and checkedAll, only whether it ran all its steps. Checking stops at the first step with problems, so false means later steps did not run and the problems listed may not be all. Checks made only on writing are outside it: sending the update checks version, Turn and permissions again against the Brief as it is then, and can still be refused, e.g. with snapshot_limit when the Brief's snapshots would exceed their total. brief_update itself makes the same checks and writes nothing when it refuses, so a section you mean to send now needs no pre-check: send it, fix what the rejection lists and send again with a new requestId. Use validateOnly to check without writing, e.g. a draft you will not send in this Turn.
## ask
kind ask needs ask:

- ask {question, reply{options?[2-8]{id, label}, freeText?: true|{prompt?}, form?{…}, choice?{a{id, label, detail?}, b{id, label, detail?}}}, gate?{taskId, step: integer}}: a question and how the user can answer.
- question: 1-500 characters. reply needs at least one of options, freeText, form or choice; otherwise the change is rejected.
- options: 2-8 buttons; each sends one prefilled reply message to you. freeText: true, or {prompt} to label the text box. choice: two approaches a and b.

- form {id, title≤160, description?≤1000, fields[1-8]{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="text", placeholder?≤160, default?{value≤2000, source≤160}}|{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="single", options[2-12]{id, label≤160, description?≤1000}, default?{value, source≤160}}|{id, label≤160, required, description?≤1000, type="multi", options[2-12]{id, label≤160, description?≤1000}, default?{value[≤12](string), source≤160}}}: One bounded form: id, title, optional description and 1-8 fields. Each field has id, type (text/single/multi), label, required and optional description. Text may have placeholder. Choices have 2-12 options with stable id, label and optional description. An optional default is {value, source}: source says where it came from; value is text, one option id or an array of option ids. Users explicitly submit answers once to this original conversation; never use forms as native permission approval. At most 8 fields, 12 options each.

Use options for one choice and a form for several related answers, as in the decision and form examples; a review of a file, as in the review example (when and how: yuzuno_guide topic brief, "Ask for a review").

- gate {taskId, step}: only for an executor at a gate step of its task's template (step counts from 0, as executor_templates_list lists them): the approval it asks for. Core refuses it from any other Agent (gate_not_yours) or for a step that is not a gate (gate_step_unknown). The executor's Overview shows the ask at that step and the user can answer it there too; the step is done once the ask is replied.

The user's answer reaches you as an ordinary message quoting the section. The ask then shows "replied": it leaves Needs you, and brief_get lists it in you.repliedAsks (key, title, repliedAt, the reply in short, updatedSinceReply). It stays until you resolve it with {op:"resolve", key}; nothing closes it for you.

When to resolve: a preference or information you asked for, once you have taken it in; an action the reply authorizes, only after that action is confirmed done and its result is on the existing Task or a Brief section. A green CI or a whole Task being done is not that action. While it runs, or after it fails, keep the ask replied and report progress on the Task or Brief: edit keeps it replied, while put asks it again. Ask again only when the user has something new to decide. A reply executes nothing by itself: act on what the user has authorized, an explicit reply included, without asking for it again, and never infer a retry, merge or wider permission from an answer that does not grant it.
brief_get's you.openAsks counts your unresolved asks, open or replied.
Answers never execute actions: nothing in a Brief merges, deploys or approves; Core approvals stay separate.
## content

body is {root, elements}: elements maps ids (a letter, then letters, digits, - or _) to {type, props, children?, visible?} (visible: see interactive). root names the one BriefBody. The elements form one tree: each used once, at most 6 levels and 32 components, at most 64000 bytes of compact JSON. Only BriefBody, Group, Columns and Tabs have children. In each component's props, ? marks an optional prop, [a-b] an array's item count, ≤n a string's longest length in characters and ="a"|"b" the only values a prop takes. Components:

- BriefBody {summary?{lead, visual?, conditions?, size?="small"|"wide"|"large"}, details?[1-32](string)}: The root of every section body. summary and details name some of its own children by id; see Layout below. Children: at most 32.
- Group {title?≤160, tone?="plain"|"accent"|"muted"}: A group of components with an optional title. tone accent or muted tints its background, e.g. for a summary across the top. Children: at most 24.

- Columns {widths?[2-4](integer)}: Lays out its children side by side, each child one column (usually a Group). widths gives their relative widths, e.g. [2, 1]; equal without it. A narrow window stacks the columns in the order given. Children: 2-4, one per column.

- Tabs {id, label?≤160}: Pages the reader switches between, one tab each, e.g. news, papers and policy: each child is a page, its Group's title on its tab. label names them all for screen readers, e.g. Categories. The first page shows first. A card's summary never shows it: no summary names a Tabs or a block in one; it shows on the report page, and wherever the whole body does. Children: 2-6 titled Groups, one per page.

- Markdown {text≤64000}: GitHub-flavoured Markdown: paragraphs, lists, links, tables and fenced code or log excerpts. HTML written in it is sanitized: scripts, event handlers, images, forms, buttons, frames and styles are removed, so write Markdown, not HTML.
- Math {tex≤4000, display?}: A KaTeX formula; display:true sets it on its own line.
- Checklist {title?≤160, items[1-30]{id, text≤1000, done}}: Items with done flags.
- Plan {title?≤160, steps[1-30]{id, text≤1000, state="todo"|"doing"|"done"|"blocked"}}: Ordered steps, each todo, doing, done or blocked.

- Findings {title?≤160, items[1-30]{id, source≤160, severity="info"|"low"|"medium"|"high"|"critical", text≤2000}}: Review or analysis findings, each with its source (file, tool or reviewer) and severity.
- Metrics {items[1-12]{label≤160, value, unit?≤30, previous?, detail?≤2000}}: Key numbers with optional unit; give previous (the value in your last version) to show the change when both are numbers.

- Table {id, title?≤160, columns[1-12]{key, label≤160}, rows[≤200]{id, cells{<key>: string≤500|number|boolean|null}, sourceIds?[≤12](string)}, selectable?}: A searchable sortable table; every row has a cell for every column key. title defaults to "Table".

- LiveRefs {layout?="chips"|"list", items[1-50]{kind="task"|"pr"|"ci"|"job"|"run"|"review"|"agent"|"machine", id, label?≤160, note?≤200}}: References that Yuzuno shows with their current state: task (e.g. T-12, or a Project task key such as YN-3), pr (owner/repo#12), ci (run id), job, run (a run of stages: the runId job_run_submit returned; Yuzuno shows its status and how many stages are done), review (review id), agent or machine id. layout list shows one row per item in your order, with a short note of yours; for tasks Yuzuno fills in the title, state, assignee and last update, so write none of them. While Home cannot read Core, a list keeps the states it read last and says they are out of date.
- Attachments {items[1-12]{name, caption?≤500}}: Shows this section's attachments by name with optional captions.
- Sources {items[≤30]{id, label≤160, href≤2000}}: Explicit HTTPS or local file references; Table rows cite them by id in sourceIds.

- Collection {id, title?≤160, layout="carousel"|"grid"|"list", items[2-30]{id, title≤120, text?≤200, meta?≤160, image?, alt?≤160, href?≤2000, tags?[≤4](string≤160)}}: Items of one kind, each a title with an optional picture (an image attachment of this section), line, source or time (meta), https link and tags, laid out as a carousel (one page each, side by side), a grid of tiles or a list of rows. On the report page a grid or list whose items have tags can be filtered by tag, and a list searched.
- LineChart, BarChart, ScatterChart: see charts.
- ResearchDesk: see research.
- NumberInput, Switch, Segmented, Calc, Button, Diagram, Figure, Steps, Timeline: see interactive.
Table and chart ids, row ids, item ids and column keys are unique. Sources hrefs are http(s) URLs or local file paths (optionally :line); Table rows cite them by id in sourceIds.

LiveRefs show Core's records, read each time Home reads the Brief and never saved in your section: your label names the item, and its state is the record's own (a task's board state, a Job's run state), not whether an Agent is working on it now. An item Core does not know shows as not found: check its id. One Core could not read just then shows as couldn't read: leave it, a later read shows its state again. A state you write in Plan, Table, Metrics or Markdown is your account as of when you wrote it (a status's asOf), not live: for the current state of a task, PR, CI run or Job, reference it, as the overview example does with its Job.

Form follows the information, unless the user or Project prefers another: a real screenshot or a labelled sketch (say which) for a UI or layout change, a chart of measured data for quantities and how they relate, a short sentence for a single state. The result, compare and decision examples show each; image shows a screenshot.

Collection: items of one kind (news, papers, projects, pictures), 2-30, each with a title and, as it has them, an image, text (one line), meta (its source or time, e.g. "News · 07:40"), an https href its title opens in a new window, and up to 4 tags. image names an image attachment of this section (see attachments), which the Collection shows, so it needs no Attachments block; alt says what it shows. A section has at most 12 attachments, so at most 12 pictures; an item without one shows its text alone. layout: carousel is one page per item side by side, a picture over its text, for a few the reader looks at one by one; grid is tiles to browse and compare; list is rows for many results. Nothing turns pages by itself. As the summary's visual, a wide or large card shows a carousel whole, a grid's first row (two rows on a large card) and a list's first 3 rows (8 on a large card), and a small card its first item, each with how many there are. The report page shows every item; a grid or list whose items have tags shows up to 12 of them to filter by, and a list a search of titles, text and meta.

Layout: a short answer first, the first Markdown on its own or in a Group with tone accent, since its first paragraph is what a reader sees first; then a Columns of Groups for parts that sit side by side, as in the overview example, and a Tabs of titled Groups for parts of one kind the reader picks between (news, papers, policy), as in the tabs example. Keep each block's id across versions: edit changes one block by its id (see sections).

Home opens a report or status as a whole page. To lead it with what the reader needs first, give the BriefBody summary {lead, visual?, conditions?, size}: lead, visual and conditions are ids of the root's own blocks. lead is a Markdown with the conclusion; visual one figure (a chart, Metrics, Calc, Diagram, Figure, Steps, Timeline, Table, ResearchDesk, Collection, Attachments with one image file, or a Group of inputs the reader sets on the card, see interactive); conditions a Markdown or Checklist of what the conclusion holds under, shown with it wherever it shows. size is the room the card takes among Home's cards: small (one column: the lead and conditions, Metrics of one or two values as big numbers, a Collection's first item; any other figure is left to the page), wide (two columns, the figure beside the text: a table, a line or bar chart, more Metrics, a research desk; a Collection under it) or large (two columns, two rows: an image, a scatter chart, an HTML page). Name it with every summary, for what the summary shows, not for how much you wrote. A summary without one is still accepted (advice summary_size_missing), and Home guesses its card's size from its figure. A card with no visual shows instead the first kept image or single HTML page (.html or .htm) its Attachments show, and names up to three other files under it; an HTML page shows working on the card, in the same sandbox as its Preview, and opens large from there. A report whose body holds only its lead (one paragraph), the card's picture and files, and its conditions is the whole report: its card has no Open report. The user may give a card they pinned to their widgets another size there; your card keeps yours. The page shows them first, once, and the rest in your order; nothing is copied, so keep each in one place. details lists titled Groups of supporting detail (a method, an appendix) that start folded under their title; nothing else folds. Without summary, the page shows the body in your order. Either way, Sources and Attachments directly under the root show beside the body (after it on a narrow screen), never behind a click.

Advice: an accepted brief_update, or a validateOnly check that passes, may carry up to 3 advice {code, path, reason, guide} on the report and status sections it sent; for an edit, only on the blocks it replaced. They are adjustable hints from lengths and counts (limits.advice), not a score or a limit: nothing is cut, refused or rewritten, the update stays accepted, and a section whose title and captions already say enough may stay as it is. Characters are Unicode code points. Codes:
- summary_size_missing: A BriefBody summary with no size: Home can only guess its card's size from its figure.
- long_markdown: A Markdown block over 1200 characters, or a section whose Markdown is over 3000 characters in all.
- summary_may_be_missing: A Table or chart and no non-empty Markdown, Findings or Metrics block.
- duplicate_ref: One LiveRefs or Sources block that names the same target twice.
- many_refs: Over 12 LiveRefs and Sources entries in one section, each target counted once per block.

- BarChart {id, title?≤160, x{label≤160, unit?≤30}, y{label≤160, unit?≤30}, series?[1-12]{name≤160, points[1-500]([2-2]())}, data?{attachment, x≤80, series[1-12]{name≤160, column≤80}}}: A bar chart from inline points or a data attachment; x is usually a label. Each point is an [x, y] pair. title defaults to "Chart".

- ScatterChart {id, title?≤160, x{label≤160, unit?≤30}, y{label≤160, unit?≤30}, series?[1-12]{name≤160, points[1-500]([2-2]())}, data?{attachment, x≤80, series[1-12]{name≤160, column≤80}}}: A scatter plot with numeric x, from inline points or a data attachment. Each point is an [x, y] pair. title defaults to "Chart".
Give exactly one of:
- series: inline points [[x, y], ...], at most 500 points across all series. LineChart and BarChart x is a number or a short label; ScatterChart x is a number; y is a number.

- data: {attachment, x, series:[{name, column}]}. attachment names one of this section's attachments whose path ends in .csv, .json or .jsonl (CSV with a header row, a JSON array of objects, or one JSON object per line). x and each column name a CSV header or JSON key. Yuzuno reads the snapshot taken when you wrote the section and downsamples each series to at most 5000 points.

## research

- ResearchDesk {schema="research/1", title?≤160, claims[1-12]{id, title≤160, statement≤1200, status="supported"|"conditional"|"unsupported"|"open", primary?, plots?[≤8](string), paper?[≤16]{label≤160, cite{source, lines?}}, conditions?[≤16]{id, text≤1000}, statements?[≤16]{id, stance="can"|"cannot", kind="criterion"|"interpretation"|"exploratory", text≤1200, basis?[≤16](string)}, dependsOn?[≤16]{id, version}}, plots[≤8]{id, title≤160, unit?≤30, digits?, scale?, interval?≤160, reference?{value, label≤160}, diffLabel?≤160, partsLabel?≤160, rows[1-40]{id, label≤160, group?≤160, compare?, estimate{value, low?, high?, definition?{id, version}, cite?{source, lines?}}, parts?[1-4]{id, label≤160, estimate{value, low?, high?, definition?{id, version}, cite?{source, lines?}}}, note?≤1200}}, sources[≤40]{id, label≤160, kind="data"|"paper"|"notes"|"script"|"other", snapshot?, task?{taskId, activitySeq}, location?≤400, revision?, sha256?}, definitions?[≤12]{id, title≤160, versions[1-6]{version, text≤1200, frozenAt?, cite{source, lines?}, change?≤1200}}, revisions?[≤12]{id, claim, target≤160, definition{id, from, to}, basis="declared"|"author", draft≤1200}, plans?[≤6]{id, title≤160, question≤1200, state="candidate"|"approved"|"done", inputs?[≤16]{label≤160, source?}, params?[≤16]{name≤160, value≤160}, compute="none"|"cpu"|"gpu", budget?≤160, outputs?[≤16](string≤160), notProduced?[≤16](string≤160), links?[≤4]{kind="task"|"job"|"run", id, label?≤160}, note?≤1200}}: A research question as claims with intervals, the conditions and limits of what may be said, the sources and definitions each number rests on, and candidate next steps; see research.

One block for a research question: what each claim may and may not say, the numbers and intervals it rests on, under which conditions, from which sources and under which definition, and what could be done next. The reader selects a claim, a row or one of its parts; the block keeps that selection across your later versions while the ids stay. Use your own ids and keep them across versions. Row and part ids share one namespace across the whole desk, every plot included: each is used once, so two plots cannot both have a row "a", nor a part the id of a row.

Numbers: each value, low and high is a literal, shown as provided by you, or {from, pointer}: a JSON Pointer into one of this section's attachments whose path ends in .json, or {from, row, column} for one whose path ends in .csv or .tsv (a header row, then one row per line): row names 1 to 4 columns and the text each holds, e.g. {"sport": "alpha", "d": "2"}, every one of which must match, and column is the column the number is in. Cells compare as text as written, without the spaces around them: "2" does not match "2.0". No matching row shows as missing, two or more as ambiguous, never a guess; a cell that is not a number shows as such. Yuzuno reads it from the snapshot taken when you wrote the section and shows it as read from that snapshot, with the snapshot's SHA-256 and when it was taken; a pointer that finds no number shows as such. Neither is a check of the research: a snapshot read only says the number is in that file. Yuzuno does not compare your text with the numbers or round anything for you; digits sets how many decimals are displayed, and scale a factor for display only (e.g. 100 for a fraction shown as percentage points, with unit saying so): the value as the file has it is shown beside it. At most 400 numbers read from attachments per desk.

Sources: each source may name a snapshot (an attachment of this section); location, revision and sha256 are your description, shown as yours and never read. revision is a commit hash, 7 to 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters (not a branch, tag or other name); sha256 is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. A source with a snapshot shows the snapshot's SHA-256 and when it was taken, and whether your sha256 is the same file content; that is file identity, not a result. Yuzuno does not look at the file again later: the snapshot is as of when you wrote the section. A source may instead name a Task research record, task: {taskId, activitySeq} (taskId T-N or a Project task key such as YN-3; any key the task had still names it), one you or another Agent wrote with task_comment research: it is shown as the task keeps it (its type, title, producer and version) and needs no attachment; that is the record's identity, not a check of it. Removing the section leaves the record on its task.

Definitions: an analysis definition keeps every version you give, each citing a source with a snapshot (with lines when part of a file) or a source naming a Task method record. A version's number names one content: to change a definition, add a new version; Core refuses a version whose text, citation or cited file differs from the same version of the same desk (the element) in this section's previous version; each desk's definitions are its own. Estimates name the definition version they use; rows with the same compare id under two versions show side by side as before and after. Removing old versions is allowed, but the history then shows only what remains.

Claims: primary is the id of one row of the desk's plots (plots[].rows[].id), the row the claim leads with; not a plot or part id. plots lists plot ids. status (supported, conditional, unsupported, open) and statements are your reading and show as yours; kind criterion is a statistical criterion, interpretation your interpretation, exploratory an exploratory observation. dependsOn names the definition versions a claim rests on; when a newer version exists, the claim shows as affected through that declared dependency only. revisions are your drafts of changed wording for a claim (basis declared, or author when the author confirmed the dependency); Yuzuno shows them for review and never applies them.

Plans: candidate next steps as a preview: the question, inputs, parameters, compute (none, cpu or gpu), budget, what they produce and what they do not. Nothing runs from the block, and opening it runs nothing; links name existing tasks, Jobs or runs of stages (kind run, the runId job_run_submit returned), shown with their current state like LiveRefs (they count toward the 50 LiveRefs of a section). A Job that succeeded is not a result that holds.
Limits: 12 claims, 8 plots, 40 rows per plot, 4 parts per row, 40 sources, 12 definitions with 6 versions each, 12 revisions, 6 plans, 16 entries per list, 1200 characters per text.
## interactive

Inputs let the reader try values on Home's card and on the report page: a quantity they will scale or split (servings, a bill, a budget), a case to switch on or off, one of a few views; a Calc works out numbers from them. What the reader sets stays in their window: it is never saved, never sent to you and never runs anything, and a new version of the section, or a reload, starts again from the values you wrote. When you need the reader's answer, ask with an ask.

When to draw: draw only when the reader would do something with it. A quantity the reader will scale or split (servings, a bill, a budget, a what-if) is NumberInput, Segmented or Switch with a Calc, starting at the common case. A process with a decision or a loop, or more than four steps that branch, is a Diagram. The parts of a physical thing, or a screenshot with callouts, is a Figure over an image attachment. A procedure the reader follows step by step is Steps (walk for four or more steps done with busy hands). Three or more dated events are a Timeline; a planned date says it is planned. A single fact, a yes or no, a number or a short status is one sentence of Markdown, no component; and never draw what Core already shows (a task's state is a LiveRefs item). The reader's values never reach you: ask with an ask when you need an answer.

- NumberInput {name, label≤160, value, min, max, step?, prefix?≤8, unit?≤8, digits?, control?="stepper"|"slider"|"both", detail?≤300}: A number the reader sets with - and + (stepper), a slider or both, between min and max; it declares the variable name, starting at value.
- Switch {name, label≤160, value, detail?≤300}: An on/off switch; it declares the variable name, true or false, starting at value.

- Segmented {name, label?≤160, value, options[2-6]{value, label≤160}}: One choice among 2-6 options, as a row of segments; it declares the variable name, starting at value, one of the options' values.

- Calc {title?≤160, layout?="list"|"metrics", items[1-12]{id, label≤160, expr≤240, when?≤240, prefix?≤8, unit?≤8, digits?, emphasis?, detail?≤300}}: Numbers worked out from the section's variables as the reader sets them: each item's expr is a formula, shown with its label; when hides the item while it is false. layout list (the default) is a two-column list, metrics shows them as Metrics.
- Button {label≤160, tone?="plain"|"accent"}: A button that sets variables to fixed values when pressed, e.g. Reset; its element's on says which (see interactive).

- Diagram {title?≤160, caption?≤160, direction?="down"|"right", select?, nodes[1-40]{id, label≤60, shape?="box"|"round"|"diamond", tone?="plain"|"accent"|"ok"|"warn"|"muted", detail?≤600}, edges[≤60]{from, to, label?≤24, style?="solid"|"dashed"}}: A flowchart or a diagram of parts, as nodes and the edges between them; Yuzuno lays it out and draws it. A node's detail shows when the reader selects it; select names a variable that holds the selected node's id.

- Figure {image, alt≤160, caption?≤160, select?, hotspots[1-12]{id, label≤160, x, y, detail?≤600}}: An image attachment of this section with numbered hotspots at x and y, percentages of its width and height from its top left; the reader selects one to read its detail. select names a variable that holds the selected hotspot's id.

- Steps {title?≤160, mode?="list"|"walk", steps[1-30]{id, title≤160, text?≤600, time?≤24}}: Steps to follow, in order, each with a title and an optional text and time. mode walk shows one at a time, with Back and Next.

- Timeline {title?≤160, items[1-30]{id, at≤32, title≤160, text?≤600, state?="done"|"now"|"next"}}: Dated events in order, each done, now or next; across where the window is wide, down where it is narrow. The reader opens one to read its text.

Variables: each input declares one, under its name (a letter a-z, then up to 31 letters or digits, e.g. guests), starting at the input's value: a NumberInput's a number, a Switch's true or false, a Segmented's its options' values, all numbers or all texts, each once, value one of them. A name is declared once per section, at most 16 in all. A section's variables are its own; its card and its page each keep theirs.

NumberInput: min is less than max and value lies between them; step (default 1) takes at most 100000 steps from min to max; digits is how many decimals are shown (default: as many as step, min or max has); control stepper (the default: - and + beside the number), slider, or both. prefix and unit (at most 8 characters) are shown before and after the number, e.g. "¥" or "g".

visible, beside type and props, shows a block only while a condition on the variables holds; only a block inside a Group has one, as the root's own blocks are always shown. A condition is {"$state": "/<name>"}, true while a Switch is on, or with one comparison: eq or neq a value of the variable's kind (for a Segmented, one of its options' values), or gt, gte, lt or lte a number, for a number variable. not: true negates it. An array means all of its conditions hold; {"$and": [...]} and {"$or": [...]} combine conditions and each other: at most 8 conditions and 3 levels. Nothing else is read: no $item, $index, $cond, $bindState or $computed, and no expression in props.

Calc formulas: expr gives a number and when true or false, from numbers (12, 0.5), true, false, "texts" (at most 64 characters), the section's variables and this Calc's earlier items by id (when may also use the item's own), with + - * / % ^ (power, right to left: -2^2 is -4), < <= > >= == !=, && || !, cond ? a : b, parentheses and the functions round(1-2), floor(1), ceil(1), abs(1), sqrt(1), min(2-4), max(2-4), clamp(3); round(x, d) rounds to d decimals (0-6) as written, halves away from zero, so round(1.005, 2) is 1.01 and round(-2.5) is -3. Arithmetic and order take numbers, && || ! take true or false, and a text only sits beside == or != with a text or a Segmented's variable on its other side. Nothing else: no =, no . or [ ], no other names or functions. At most 240 characters, 80 parts and 8 levels each, 48 formulas per section, 12 items per Calc. An item id is a name like a variable's, unique in its Calc and none of the section's variables. Numbers are shown with digits decimals in the reader's language (default up to 2); one that cannot be computed (a division by zero, the square root of a negative) shows a dash with its reason, and money is best rounded with round in its last step.

Button: its element has on: {"press": action or a list of 1-4}, each {"action": "setState", "params": {"statePath": "/<name>", "value": v}}, where v is a value that variable can take (a Segmented's option, a NumberInput's number from min to max). Nothing else runs from a Button, and no other block takes on.

Diagram: you give nodes and edges only; Yuzuno lays them out (top to bottom, or left to right with direction right, turned top to bottom where the window is too narrow) and draws them in the reader's theme. Use it for a process with a decision or a loop, or more than four steps that branch, and for the parts of a thing and how they connect. A node's shape diamond is a decision, round a start or an end; tone accent marks the path that matters, ok and warn an outcome, muted what is out of scope. An edge's label (at most 24 characters) names the branch, e.g. yes or no; style dashed is optional or later. An edge may go back to an earlier node (a loop); none goes from a node to itself, and two nodes have at most one edge in each direction. At most 40 nodes and 60 edges; node ids are unique. The reader selects a node by pointer or keyboard to read its detail (at most 600 characters). select names a variable that then holds the selected node's id ("" while none is), for visible and Calc to read: one of the Diagram's own, or a Segmented's of texts with an option for every node id, so the segments and the nodes select together.

Figure: image names an image attachment of this section (see attachments), which the Figure shows, so it needs no Attachments block; alt says what it shows. Each hotspot is a numbered marker at x and y, percentages of the image's width and height from its top left corner, listed with its label under the image; at most 12. The reader selects one to read its detail, and select works as a Diagram's, with the hotspots' ids: e.g. a Segmented naming the parts of a machine and its photo's hotspots select together.

## attachments
- attachments [≤12]{name, path?≤4096, url?≤2000, caption?≤500}: Files and links of this section.
- Give exactly one of path or url. name is unique in the section; the body refers to it.

- path: an absolute path on the machine where Core runs. Files up to 25 MB are kept as a snapshot when you write the section; larger files and directories are only referenced and marked "may have changed".
- url: an https link, shown as a link only, never embedded.
Images, data files (CSV, JSON, JSONL), PDF, logs and text (the last 200 lines are previewed) and links. Show them in the body with Attachments; charts read data files (see charts).

An HTML page (one self-contained .html or .htm file) shows working on its card and in its Preview, in a sandbox: its scripts run, but it makes no requests and cannot reach Home, its storage or the reader's other pages, submit forms, open windows or move Home. Three messages pass between it and Home, nothing else. Home posts {"type": "yuzuno:theme", "vars": {"--paper", "--ink", "--line", "--accent-ink", "--green", "--font"}, "scheme": "light" or "dark"} to it when it loads and when the reader's theme changes; using them is up to the page. parent.postMessage({type: "yuzuno:height", px}, "*") sets the height of its card's frame (120-1600 px). parent.postMessage({type: "yuzuno:send", text}, "*") offers the reader one message for you, the section's author (at most 2000 characters; a longer one is ignored, a newer one replaces it): Home shows it under the page and sends it as the reader's reply from Home only if they press Send. Nothing else the page does reaches you. Example: <script>addEventListener("message", (e) => { if (e.data?.type !== "yuzuno:theme") return; for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(e.data.vars)) document.documentElement.style.setProperty(name, value); document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = e.data.scheme; }); const fit = () => parent.postMessage({type: "yuzuno:height", px: document.documentElement.scrollHeight}, "*"); addEventListener("load", fit); document.querySelector("#done").onclick = () => parent.postMessage({type: "yuzuno:send", text: "My score: " + score}, "*");</script>

Registration alone saves/references a file; it does not show it. Show every attachment of a put where it belongs: in a reachable Attachments.items entry with the exact name, as LineChart/BarChart/ScatterChart data.attachment, or as a Figure's image or a Collection item's image. A ResearchDesk uses the attachments it names too: each sources[].snapshot and each number's from. Markdown/Sources mentions and disconnected blocks do not count; a put's registration nothing uses is added to an Attachments block at the end of the root and listed in repairs (showed_attachment), never refused. Multiple components may use the same name. Chart data use does not also display a file preview; add Attachments if that is wanted.

An edit is never repaired that way: one that removes a previously used attachment's last reference is refused with unused_attachment, which leaves the old content, snapshots and ask state unchanged. Add a reachable Attachments block, reference a supported data file from a chart, or put the section without that registration. Checks use the final merged body, not just an edit's blocks. Existing sections/history remain readable. An unrelated edit keeps already-unused old registrations. A put checks every registration again, old ones included, and shows an unused one.

## limits
- Brief: 12 topics (one card per open Task not counted), 4 subs per topic; seen reports stay 30 days.
- Body: 64000 bytes of compact JSON, 32 components, 6 levels; BriefBody 32 children, Group 24, Columns 2-4, Tabs 2-6.
- Markdown: each fenced code or log block 200 lines. Math: 4000 characters.
- Checklist, Plan and Findings: 30 items each. Metrics: 12. Sources: 30.
- Table: 200 rows, 12 columns. Collection: 2-30 items, 4 tags each.
- Charts: 12 series; inline 500 points in total; data attachments downsampled to 5000 points per series.
- LiveRefs: 50 per section. Attachments: 12 per section; snapshots 25 MB per file, 1 GB per Brief (oldest history pruned first).
- ask: 2-8 options; form 1-8 fields, 2-12 options each.
Over a limit, the rejection says what to keep here and what to leave on the Task.
## errors

A rejected brief_update lists problems {code, path, reason, guide}: at most 5 for each section's format and at most 10 in all. moreProblems says how many more Core found past 10; problems past a section's 5 are not found or counted. path is where in your change (e.g. body.elements.log.props.text); reason says what to change; guide names the brief_guide part to read. Fix them all and call brief_update again with a new requestId.
- invalid_section: The change is not an object.
- unknown_field: A field the format does not have.
- missing_field: A required field is missing.
- invalid_field: A value of the wrong type, format or range.
- invalid_key: The key is not topic or topic/sub.
- unknown_component: A component type outside the catalog.
- too_many: A list over its limit.
- too_long: A text over its limit.
- too_large: The body is over 64000 bytes of compact JSON.
- block_too_long: A Markdown code or log block is over 200 lines.
- too_many_points: An inline chart has over 500 points.
- too_many_refs: The section has over 50 LiveRefs.
- ask_required: kind ask without ask.
- ask_without_reply: An ask without options, freeText, form or choice.
- status_required: kind status without status.
- misplaced_field: ask or status on a section of another kind.
- root: The root is not a BriefBody.
- component_count: Fewer than 1 or more than 32 components.
- not_a_tree: Elements are shared, cyclic or deeper than 6 levels.
- missing_component: A child names a missing element.
- extra_root: More than one BriefBody.
- unused_component: An element not reachable from the root.
- summary: A BriefBody summary whose lead, visual or conditions is not one of the root's own children of the right type, or names a block twice.
- details: A BriefBody details entry that is not a titled Group among the root's own children, is named twice or is part of the summary.
- columns_widths: Columns widths that do not match its children.
- duplicate_id: Two items, rows, columns, series or components share an id.
- row_mismatch: A Table row's cells do not match its columns.
- invalid_source: A Sources href that is not an http(s) URL or local path, or a duplicate source id.
- missing_source: A sourceIds entry with no matching source.
- chart_data: A chart without exactly one of series or data.
- missing_attachment: A name not in the section's attachments.

- unused_attachment: An attachment an edit leaves unused by a reachable Attachments block, chart data, Figure, Collection or ResearchDesk (a put's unused one is shown instead, see Repairs); add a reference or remove its registration with put.
- chart_attachment: A chart attachment that is not a CSV, JSON or JSONL file with a path.
- attachment_location: An attachment without exactly one of path or url, or with a path that is not absolute or a url that is not https.
- duplicate_attachment: Two attachments share a name.
- missing_reference: A ResearchDesk id that names no claim, plot, row, part, source, definition version or plan of that desk.
- research_attachment: A ResearchDesk number read from an attachment of the wrong kind: a JSON Pointer needs a .json file, a CSV row a .csv or .tsv file, each with a path.
- unsaved_definition: A ResearchDesk definition version citing a source with neither a snapshot nor a Task method record.
- definition_order: A ResearchDesk revision whose definition versions do not go from older to newer.
- too_many_values: A ResearchDesk reading over 400 numbers from attachments.

- formula: A Calc expr or when that does not parse, names something that is neither a variable of the section nor an earlier item, gives the wrong type, or is over its limits; the reason says at which character (see interactive).

- ask_only: Your current Project permission allows only your own valid asks, removing your own older sections, and optional noChange. A Project's leads edit Home; the user chooses them. Read brief_get you.capabilities and keep internal progress in tasks and mail.
- gate_not_yours, gate_step_unknown: an ask's gate names a task you are not the executor of, or a step of its template that is not a gate (see ask).
- invalid_task: task names no Task, a Task of another Project or an archived one, or comes from a member who is not a lead (see sections).
- not_card_responsible: an executor's report or status sub-topic outside the card of the Task it is the current executor of (see sections).

Repairs: when a section fails these checks for a slip Core can fix without guessing, Core repairs it and accepts the update instead: the answer (and a validateOnly check that passes) lists repairs {code, path, reason, guide}, at most 10 in all (moreRepairs counts the rest), a section that needs more than 8 is refused as sent, and Home marks the section while a repair stays: a put replaces them all; an edit removes those of the blocks it replaces, and those of the section as a whole (its tree, the root's layout, an ask's options) stay until a put. Send it right next time: the repairs say what Core changed. Outside the body Core repairs only an ask's reply options (reply_options), and a put's unused registration is shown in the body, never changed or removed: it never repairs key, kind, title, the ask's question or its other replies, status, time or an attachment's registration, nor an ask without a usable reply, anything over a limit, a reference to a file, source or research record, a ResearchDesk or Sources block, or content a component needs and you did not give (a Finding's source). When the repaired section still fails, the rejection lists the problems of the section as you sent it. Codes:
- component_to_markdown: An unknown component without children became a Markdown block of its text, HTML-escaped; one with no text was removed.
- component_to_group: An unknown component with children, or a BriefBody below the root, became a Group.
- renamed_field: A field given another name, or put outside props, was moved to the name the component uses (e.g. Findings file to source).
- dropped_field: A field the component does not have was removed.
- filled_id: A missing id was filled in, or one used twice was made unique.
- normalized_value: A value in another letter case, or a listed synonym (Plan in_progress, completed, pending), became the value the component uses.
- filled_default: A Finding without severity got info; a Table row's missing cell became empty.
- reply_options: Ask reply options given as text, or with other field names, became {id, label}.
- fixed_tree: A child naming no element was removed; an element nothing showed was added at the end of the root (removed, for an edit that unlinked it); or the root was set to the body's BriefBody.
- dropped_layout: Columns widths, a BriefBody summary slot or a details entry that did not fit was removed.
- showed_attachment: A put's registered attachment that nothing showed was added to an Attachments block under the root.

Core also rejects version_conflict (a section you change was written after the version you read, or expectedVersion is ahead of the Brief; other sections' writes don't count; the rejection includes latest: the sections you change as they are now and an index: merge and retry), no_active_turn (call it during your turn), unknown_element and edit_root (an edit naming a block the section does not have, or its root), patch_path and patch_test (a patch operation whose path or from is not in the body, an @<id> naming no item or two among them, or a test whose value differs: nothing is changed), definition_changed (a ResearchDesk definition version whose text, citation or cited file or record differs from the section's previous version; see research), unsaved_definition also when Core kept no snapshot of a definition's cited file or the cited Task record is not a method record it can read, and changes that break owner, topic or open-ask rules.
